description.en: The aim of the experiment is to verify Norton’s Theorem.
The Instructions button provides step-by-step guidance for performing the simulation.
The AI Guide assists you at each stage of the simulation.
The Check button verifies the current circuit connections. If a wire is incorrect, click its numbered label to remove it. Switch the source on only after the connections are verified.
The Auto Connect button creates all required connections for the current case automatically.
The Add button records the displayed reading in the observation table.
The Calculate button fills the recorded resistance and source values in the theoretical verification panel so you can enter the Norton values and verify the load current.
The Reset button returns the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The Print button prints the completed simulation page.
Set R1, R2, R3 and RL with the resistance sliders. Once all four values are fixed, the sliders lock so the same resistance values are used throughout the experiment.

The DC power supply provides the circuit voltage. Switch it on after the current circuit connections are verified, then set a voltage from 0 to 15 V. The voltage slider locks after its value is fixed.
The ammeter displays the Norton current (IN) and the load current (IL) in milliamperes for the relevant circuit cases.
The digital multimeter operates in resistance mode to measure the Norton equivalent resistance (RN) in kΩ while the independent voltage source is deactivated.
Build each required circuit by dragging wires between the numbered terminals, or use Auto Connect. Check the connections before switching on the supply.
The observation table records the measured Norton resistance (RN), Norton current (IN), load resistance (RL), and observed load current (IL).
Open this section to review the equations used to determine Norton resistance (RN), Norton current (IN), and load current (IL).
After clicking Calculate, enter IN, RN and RL in their allowed ranges. The panel calculates IL with the displayed Norton formula and compares it with the observed load current.
After completing the observation table and theoretical verification, generate the summarized simulation report.
